Author: @dreamfeatherbolts
Content:
It's actually BAD for you to lose too much weight too quickly, how much depends on just how big you are, that's why the doctor sets goals. I assume that's the amount he's determined that if they lose MORE THAN it could be unhealthy for them and dangerous, it's a measuring stick not just about whether they're willing to put in the effort but also to ensure that if they ARE willing that they're not actually harming themselves while doing it.

A good average weight to lose per week is 1-2lbs, especially if you don't have a LOT of extra that you'll be losing. Some of it is also a mental thing as well, as studies show those who gradually lose weight  rather than those quickly losing it are more likely to have longterm success. Likely because the gradual ones have had actual lifestyle changes they had to stick to for long periods of time to lose that weight, whereas rapid ones may have simply done crash diets or water loss etc that's meant to be a quick "one and done" thing.

Author: @DrBellaLJ
Content:
I hate to shatter Ken’s belief that he didn’t eat junk food on the way to Houston (when moving). On the first trip to Houston for his visit with Dr. Now, Paul ate an insane amount of food every few hours. They were not on the road 1.5 hours and he made them stop at McDonald’s where he ordered enough food for a large family (multiple double quarter pounders with cheese, chicken sandwiches, 10 piece nuggets, fries, a dozen cookies, and more). He stated that to motivate himself, his goal was to stop every 100 miles for a food reward. I will never understand why if you’re heading to a weight loss surgeon, you would eat so much food that you would gain 10+ pounds on the way there! I was hoping that because this was the “wholesome story” that he would be the person who didn’t eat an insane amount while heading to Houston to see Dr. Now, but I watched the full episode last night and was disappointed at the amount of food he ate while on the way. He had the same complaints. The person states that they are in pain that they need to eat. Even his best friend, who is driving, was disturbed by the amount of food he was consuming on the trip there. He stuffed so many breakfast burritos in his mouth one morning in the hotel that his friend looked like she was going to cry. I got nauseated watching him stuff the food in - it’s difficult to watch from afar, so I can only imagine how distressing it is in person.
I do feel very sad for his family, his fiancé, and her son. His fiancé went from planning their wedding had to planning his funeral instead. He was making great strides - it’s really sad. I did not expect the terrible ending on this wholesome episode (We love you, Mary!)

Author: @rosebrown6381
Content:
Hi all!  Just as an FYI, for the diet that Paul had to follow (based on my own diet getting the weight loss surgery for health issues) - he probably had to get lean protein - meaning boneless, skinless chicken or turkey breasts (no dark meats at all - and the gizzards and stuff the Dad was suggesting are Dark meat - much higher in fat), whey protein shakes and powders (a HUGE part of the weight loss surgery journey - you literally have to be on an all liquid diet of these for over a month), and some lean cuts of beef.  You are given a Protein goal for every day - and how many carbs can eat, MAX, and even an amount of veggies.  You are also given a guideline for "free" foods - foods you can use to eat when you feel hungry that don't count against the rest, but even those have limits.  And you have to cut almost all fats, oils, and sugars out.

The leg condition he has is probably lymphodema or leaking blood vessels due to poor circulation - both are common in obese people or diabetics.  (I don't know that Paul is or was diabetic, but it's quite common in people that overweight.)  If you have buildup of fluids like that, you have to have affected areas wrapped to push the 'water' back out and get the circulation moving again.  Some people even need leg pumps to help.
